changes.find: squats there solemnly, in the posture of a turkey.
changes.reason: Japanese 勿体らしく is comic-pompous self-importance beside the turkey simile, not dignity, so F9's wording preserves the tableau's joke.
changes.replace: squats there with ponderous self-importance, in the posture of a turkey.

changes.find: his rig is a soap-black cloth gown
changes.reason: "Rig" slips into modern slang against the measured formal register the reading requires, and this minimal change removes that slip without adopting R4's equally colloquial "get-up."
changes.replace: he is dressed in a soap-black cloth gown

changes.find: that Chang San's black cataract suddenly took a turn for the better, for instance, or that Li Si's impotence was healed on the spot
changes.reason: The English apposition never resolves grammatically; "how... or how..." repairs the agreement while keeping every reported fact and the hearsay tone.
changes.replace: how Chang San's black cataract suddenly took a turn for the better, for instance, or how Li Si's impotence was healed on the spot

changes.find: stroking his bamboo wife as
changes.reason: The Japanese ながら clause runs on to Liu's speech in p22; supplying "he said" restores that linkage instead of leaving a drafting fragment at the paragraph break.
changes.replace: stroking his bamboo wife as he said:

changes.find: And was himself ashamed of it.
changes.reason: English needs the subject here; adding "he" repairs a drafting slip without smoothing any authorial roughness, since the Japanese has two full sentences.
changes.replace: And he was himself ashamed of it.

changes.find: he recalled within himself that his host Liu, who would meet such an arrogant monk, was absurd.
changes.reason: 思ひ出した here is a present contemptuous judgment striking Sun, not a memory, and F2's wording keeps Sun's inwardness and the narrator's flat report of it.
changes.replace: it struck him inwardly how foolish his host Liu was to meet such an arrogant monk.

changes.find: his good friend on the wine-mound
changes.reason: "Boon companion" keeps the mock-heroic classical tag for Sun in English a reader can parse, without glossing the wine-mound itself.
changes.replace: his boon companion of the wine-mound

changes.find: should by the turn of the moment stand witness
changes.reason: "By the turn of the moment" is a calque that means nothing in English; "as things fell out" renders 当座の行きがかり plainly.
changes.replace: should as things fell out stand witness

changes.find: may seem exceedingly improvident
changes.reason: "Improvident" is ennoblement in Berman's sense, managerial where the narrator's sly dig at Liu (and, by extension, at the schooled) is blunt, and the reading requires that dig to stay.
changes.replace: may seem grossly fatuous

changes.find: is in truth for the most part the doing of the same sort of thing.
changes.reason: The nominalisation buries the narrator's dig at school education; R11's wording keeps the aside intact and only removes the extra nouns.
changes.replace: is in truth for the most part doing much the same thing.

changes.find: in the skin of the upper parts of him, face or body alike.
changes.reason: The Japanese means the sunward-facing surfaces of the bound, face-up body, not the upper body; F4 restores the posture the ordeal depends on.
changes.replace: in the skin of the upward-facing parts of him, face or body alike.

changes.find: a smarting everywhere.
changes.reason: "A smarting everywhere" forces an adverb into noun service; "all over" keeps the narrator's hedged clinical definition of the pain grammatical without prettifying it.
changes.replace: a smarting all over.

changes.find: doctored his soldiers' thirst
changes.reason: "Doctored" suggests falsifying in English; "cured" preserves the ironic medical echo of 医す in the Cao Mengde allusion.
changes.replace: cured his soldiers' thirst

changes.find: the rich fumes of wine assail his nose without pause.
changes.reason: 芬々たる酒香 is fragrant wine-aroma, and the reading requires the repeated term to stay verbally stable so the thirst is sharpened by attraction, not disgust.
changes.replace: the rich wine-aroma assails his nose without pause.

changes.find: that reek seems to grow stronger with every minute.
changes.reason: "Reek" breaks the 酒香 repetition and colours the aroma pejoratively where the Japanese repeats the same neutral word, so the network of the passage survives only with one term throughout.
changes.replace: that aroma seems to grow stronger with every minute.

changes.find: perhaps half of its generously swollen belly.
changes.reason: 応揚にふくれた is dignified amplitude, not generosity; "broadly" keeps the jar plain and avoids the jolly ennoblement.
changes.replace: perhaps half of its broadly swollen belly.

changes.find: meaning to beg the monk at his pillow to stop the cure.
changes.reason: 申込む is a flat proposal to stop, and "beg" makes Liu abject and victim-like, pre-deciding him in a way the reading forbids.
changes.replace: meaning to ask the monk at his pillow to call off the cure.

changes.find: should have ridden on such a fellow's cajolery into this idiotic suffering.
changes.reason: No English speaker rides on cajolery; R15 keeps Liu's self-reproach and register while changing only the literal-translation vehicle of 口車に乗る.
changes.replace: should have let such a fellow's patter lead him into this idiotic suffering.

changes.find: all at once it slips like a loach or something out of the dark and flies outwards with force.
changes.reason: The tactile ぬるりと is the disgust of the climax and the reading requires the earthworm-gecko-loach sequence kept visceral and unprettified.
changes.replace: all at once, slimily, like a loach or something, it slips out of the dark and flies outwards with force.

changes.find: At this the monk abruptly lifts the haunches he had settled
changes.reason: The Japanese keeps 蛮僧 at the moment of success, and dropping "barbarian" breaks the stable monk-naming the reading asks English to report plainly.
changes.replace: At this the barbarian monk abruptly lifts the haunches he had settled

declined.reason: 畑と云ふ畑は is idiomatic Japanese emphasis, and "every field that is a field" carries that emphasis in English; R1's "worthy of the name" clarifies and ennobles a tautology the text intends, so the strangeness stays.
"A handy jar" in English already reads as convenient-sized (手ごろ), and "right-sized" is clunkier than the fault it cures; jars may also "stand" at a pillow in this formal register without misleading.
R3's "with dignity, for all the world like a turkey" dignifies the monk exactly where 勿体らしく mocks his self-importance; F9's wording, taken above, keeps the author's joke in a writer's English.

Declined for now and sent up: glossing "bamboo wife" in text would be the expansion/clarification the keikaku test warns against in a story already wearing its erudition openly, but the retained-terms system is an open question awaiting the editor's ruling.

すると、その途端である is itself a short declarative sentence in the Japanese, and the reading forbids joining the short sentences elsewhere into graceful compounds; the fragment is authorial suspension, not a drafting chop.

"Haunches he had settled" is odd but comprehensible after the turkey-squat of p4 and preserves the comedy of 尻; R17's "heaves up the haunches he had settled himself upon" is more unwieldy than the wording it replaces.

Declined for now and sent up: "three sun" left bare does stop the reader, but inserting "some four inches" decides the retained-measure question the house has flagged as needing an editor's ruling, and three sun is nearer three and a half inches besides.

disagreements.choice: F9's "ponderous self-importance" is taken and R3 declined.
disagreements.faithful_side: F9: 勿体らしく is ironic comic pomposity beside the turkey simile, and "solemnly" ennobles it.
disagreements.readable_side: R3: "solemnly" plus "posture of a turkey" reads machine-like, so keep the turkey but word it as a writer would ("with dignity, for all the world like a turkey").

disagreements.choice: F7's "barbarian monk" is restored and "haunches he had settled" stands as drafted.
disagreements.faithful_side: F7: 蛮僧 must stay at the moment of success to keep the monk-naming stable.
disagreements.readable_side: R17: "lifts the haunches he had settled" is indelicate and incomprehensible to an English reader.

disagreements.choice: The text stands with "bamboo wife" unglossed until the editor rules.
disagreements.faithful_side: No faithful note; the translator's draft and the reading's keikaku caution favour leaving the retained term to context.
disagreements.readable_side: R5: an English reader will picture a human wife, so gloss the bamboo wife in text as a rattan bolster for hot nights.

disagreements.choice: "Three sun" stands unglossed until the editor rules on retained measures.
disagreements.faithful_side: No faithful note; the draft keeps the period measure stable and left to context, as with mu and the jar.
disagreements.readable_side: R18: "three sun" means nothing to an English reader at the climax and must be glossed in text or in a note.

data.say: The desk restored the draft's dropped tactile and naming details and the narrator's blunt digs, kept the monk's naming, the wine-aroma repetition, and the short declarative breaks intact against smoothing, and sent only the two retained-term glosses (bamboo wife, three sun) up for the editor's ruling.
